definition: In a direction contrary to the sun’s apparent course; counterclockwise. Traditionally, especially in Scottish folklore, to go widdershins was considered unlucky or uncanny.
etymology: It came into Scots from Middle Low German weddersinnes, meaning “against the direction”: wider meant “against,” and sin meant “way” or “course.” The word carried the old belief that the sunwise path was the fortunate one.
usage: On Halloween, the children circled the bonfire widdershins, daring one another to name what might answer from the dark.
